narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 79.1% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt—a high-risk prediction that outweighed your other qualifications.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing. You are in the first decile, while accepted students average near the sixth decile; this pushed the prediction toward bar exam failure. Your first-year class standing was the second most important factor and also pushed toward failure, again at the first decile versus an accepted-student average near the sixth. Your undergraduate GPA was the third most influential factor. At 3.10 compared with an accepted average of 3.23, it slightly leaned toward passing and offset the academic-standing concerns, but not enough to change the overall decision. Family income and full-time status were not among the main drivers.

To move forward, ask admissions for a formal review and an opportunity to explain any circumstances behind your early class rankings. Provide updated transcripts, evidence of grade improvement, or a concrete academic-support plan for bar preparation. Consider retaking the LSAT and strengthening your record before reapplying. A thoughtful appeal that addresses the model’s main concerns—especially your first- and third-year standing—is your best next step.
